title: Making GET Requests with Query Parameters
instructions: Practice making GET requests and using query parameters to filter API results. Focus on writing the correct syntax using the `requests` library.
steps: Import the `requests` library at the top of your code
Make a GET request to `'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1'` and store the response in a variable called `single_post`
Create a dictionary called `filter_params` with two key-value pairs: `'userId'` set to `1` and `'_limit'` set to `5`
Make a GET request to `'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts'` using the `filter_params` dictionary with the `params` argument, and store the response in `filtered_posts`
Create another dictionary called `search_params` with one key-value pair: `'userId'` set to `3`. Make a GET request to the same posts URL using this dictionary and store the response in `user_posts`

# Task 5: Get all posts from user 3
solution:
# Task 1: Import requests
import requests

# Task 2: Get a single post (post ID 1)
single_post = requests.get('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1')

# Task 3: Create filter parameters dictionary
filter_params = {'userId': 1, '_limit': 5}

# Task 4: Get filtered posts (userId=1, limit=5)
filtered_posts = requests.get('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts', params=filter_params)

# Task 5: Get all posts from user 3
search_params = {'userId': 3}
user_posts = requests.get('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts', params=search_params)
hints: Task 1: Use the standard import statement: import requests
Task 2: Use requests.get(url) with the full URL as a string
Task 3: Create a dictionary with two keys: 'userId' and '_limit'
Task 4: Use requests.get(url, params=dictionary) to pass query parameters
Task 4: The base URL should be 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts'
Task 5: Create search_params dictionary first, then use it in requests.get() with the params argument
Task 5: Structure: search_params = {'userId': 3} then user_posts = requests.get(url, params=search_params)
